items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: And we had the, we had the, five brass. And I think we had four reeds. Two pianists and Snagg Jones on the drum.

ctx.x: Recall, Ellix. And then we got Lee Collins, he came up. And then Snagg Jones came up, he left, he had been playing with Celestan. And then comes Tommy Ladner. Tommy Ladner came up. So you just can see how it was with New Orleans musicians. And they were close knitted and they stuck together. And the guys said, oh this guy, they called him, called him Geechies, they called him Geechies, Cam Reed. And what they were wrong, you take people like Manny Perez, and Jimmy Noon, Eddie Atkins, and George Field, all those…
I understand Lee Collins couldn't read too well.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: the next day we'd have a whistling contest between me and Snagg Jones... So when I went back to New Orleans later on with Lil Armstrong they wasn't surprised that I was playing music because Snagg used to get the rounds of the chairs and we'd play

ctx.x: They had a union then but it wasn't able to.

Yeah, well the union wasn't as strong as it is now and the president wasn't the president we have now. I think Harry Gray is one of the greatest presidents we've had. I may be a little prejudiced because I served as a board of director of Local 20 years, and three years on the trial board. This was 23 consecutive years. Are you still official? No, I was defeated. I was defeated there in December. So getting back to this band, Weatherford, it lasted a little while, about four to six weeks, closed up on a Sunday…

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: I used to could whistle, so I'd whistle anything anybody played, and so could Snagg's Joan.

ctx.x: My mother started to call me playing music. I never would have got one myself, and then she had the little horn on the bed, I never would forget that. And I stuck with it until she passed. And so that's all I could do. But I guess she could see that I wanted to play music. She could see. I used to could whistle, so I'd whistle anything anybody played, and so could Snagg's Joan. And Joe Oliver used to have me to whistle to get ideas from me. Now you might not believe that. So he had me and Snagg's to whistle, and…
You could hear them for miles. Did you ever play a little Ken flute or anything?
